translations./garage/brief: Choose any chassis and every component with no unlock requirement. Drive with the keyboard or click the ground to hand control to autonomy. The large map includes a braking straight, wet floor, sand, mud, gravel, steel deck, longitudinal grade, cross slope, and rough road.
translations./prediction/hint: The proving ground has no unlock gate. Change one component and repeat the same route to compare evidence.
translations./prediction/choices/0/feedback: The inside front wheel must steer farther than the outside wheel so all four wheels point toward a common instantaneous center of rotation.
translations./prediction/choices/1/text: Compare the speed motor and stopping distance
translations./prediction/choices/1/feedback: A higher top speed does not shorten stopping distance for free. Braking still depends on tire grip, wheel speed, and contact load.
translations./prediction/choices/2/feedback: The 16-line sensor produces 3D returns with height, intensity, and per-point timing; a projection layer then creates 2D navigation obstacles.
translations./running/normal_line: Proving vehicle: keyboard input takes over immediately; click the ground to request autonomous navigation.
translations./running/detected_line: Proving vehicle: structure detected; manual and autonomous modes both use real platform feedback.
translations./debrief/success_summary: Change one component and repeat the route to compare physical steering, speed, slip, braking, and sensing.
translations./debrief/failure_summary: If the run fails, inspect collision, trajectory, and speed evidence before changing the route or component.
translations./debrief/evidence_caption: Body pose, wheel joints, actuator commands, contact, and LiDAR data come from one deterministic simulation run.
translations./debrief/knowledge_title: One Interface Connects Different Chassis and Hardware
translations./debrief/failure_titles/timeout: Run ended: finish not reached in time
